name: Sanballat
role: Governor in Samaria who opposed Nehemiah
whenBasis: Nehemiah's governorship under Artaxerxes I; the Elephantine papyri name his sons in 407 BC.
summary: Sanballat the Horonite, who with Tobiah the Ammonite and Geshem the Arab mocked and opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding of the wall. Before the army of Samaria he jeered, “What are these feeble Jews doing?” He plotted an attack, invited Nehemiah four times to a meeting on the plain of Ono to harm him, sent an open letter accusing him of planning to be king, and hired a prophet to frighten him. A grandson of the high priest became his son-in-law; Nehemiah drove him away.
body: When the wall is complete but for its doors, the enemies switch from threats to intrigue. Nehemiah's answer to each invitation is the same: he is doing a great work and cannot come down.

later.text: A papyrus of 407 BC from Elephantine in Egypt names Delaiah and Shelemiah, “sons of Sanballat governor of Samaria,” giving him the title.

sources.title: Elephantine papyri, Cowley 30–31 (petition to Bagohi, governor of Judah, 407 BC)
sources.note: names Johanan the high priest in Jerusalem and Delaiah and Shelemiah, sons of Sanballat governor of Samaria

later.text: Horonite has been read as from Beth-horon, north-west of Jerusalem, or from Horonaim in Moab.
